_comment: Operator-harness tunables for the Gate F run (tools/gate_f/operator_harness.gd). Deliberately NOT under data/config/: nothing the game ships reads this file, and ralph/GATE_F_INSTRUMENTATION_REQUEST.md section 10 forbids touching the game's data configs. Delete the file and the harness runs on the same values, hard-coded as defaults, so a bare checkout still works.
_comment_trace_hz: route.csv sample rate. The protocol section C.2 fixes it at 2 Hz for the run that produces Gate F evidence; the key is here so a diagnostic rerun can raise it without a code edit. Raising it costs frame time -- measure with --gatef-mode=overhead and record the result rather than assuming it is free.
_comment_settle_frames: Physics frames waited after a scene boot before anything is read or pressed. 240 is what every smoke test in tests/ uses; the Meadows scatters ~130k props at stand-up and a shorter settle reads half-built terrain as a defect.
_comment_walk_budget_frames: Physics frames one move_to step may spend walking before it reports FAIL. 2400 is 40 seconds at 60 Hz. Frames spent unable to move -- a fight, a fade, a conversation -- do not count against it (stick_navigator.gd's own rule), so this is a budget on WALKING, not on wall clock.
_comment_walk_close_enough: Metres from a move_to target that count as arrived. Looser than the navigator's own 0.8 default because a Gate F anchor is a place to stand, not a switch to press.
_comment_walk_held_budget_frames: Physics frames a move_to step will wait, in total, for locomotion to come back before giving up. 3600 is a minute at 60 Hz. stick_navigator.gd's own limit is ten minutes and then false; a harness cannot afford that, because a walk that hangs produces no evidence at all -- worse than one that reports where it stopped and what was holding it. Measured on main: walking out of the spawn triggers Grandpa's opening conversation, which takes locomotion and holds it until somebody answers.
_comment_record_default_hz: Section H baseline background frame rate for a segment that does not declare its own `record_hz`. 0.1 Hz is section H's rate for journey segments outside the mandatory high-risk list -- one frame per ten seconds plus event-forced frames, enough to keep the record continuous without drowning the run directory. A segment overrides it with a top-level `record_hz`; the mandatory list uses 0.5.
_comment_record_window_hz: Rate `record_start` uses when a step names no `hz`, and the rate the overhead self-measurement tests the recorder at. 0.5 Hz is section H's mandatory-segment rate (a frame every two seconds).
_comment_record_forced_frames: Section H's 'forced frame on every JSONL event'. Left settable because it is the one part of the continuous record that scales with how eventful a segment is rather than with its length, and X08's perf audit is meant to run without capture at all. Turning it off is a deliberate, recorded choice -- the run metadata carries the frame counts either way.
_comment_perf_window_frames: Trailing window the perf field's avg/p95/max are computed over. 60 frames is one second at the physics rate, which is the shortest window a p95 means anything over.
_comment_capture_settle_frames: Process frames waited before a capture, on top of the frame_post_draw await. A capture taken on the frame a panel opens catches it mid-fade.
_comment_overhead_scene: Which scene the section 8 overhead self-measurement runs on: 'world' or 'title'. The two costs it adds up do not live in the same place. The telemetry tick costs what the SCENE costs -- it walks the party, the quest log and the point-of-interest cache -- so it belongs on the real world, and runs there headless. The recorder's cost is a framebuffer readback and a PNG encode, which scales with PIXELS rather than scene complexity, so the title scene at the capture resolution measures it honestly. Measuring the recorder on the Meadows would be better and is not available in this container: under llvmpipe six twenty-second windows did not complete in fifty minutes, and a measurement taken while the box is that saturated describes the container rather than the instrument. The note names the scene it ran on so a reader composes the two instead of being handed one number pretending to be both.
_comment_overhead_seconds: Length of each half of the section 8 overhead self-measurement (once with telemetry on, once off). 60 s each, per the request's own wording.
_comment_segment_cost_ceiling_s: Coverage defect CD-7. `wait` is priced in RENDERED frames in capture mode: _step_wait converts seconds to physics frames and under xvfb every physics frame is a rendered 1920x1080 frame. On llvmpipe at ~10.5 s per frame one {"seconds": 90} step costs about 15.75 hours, and X07 stopped at step 184 of 266 with two of them still ahead of it -- roughly 31 more hours. The pre-flight measures what a frame costs on THIS box, prices the whole step-script against it, and refuses to start a segment predicted over this ceiling. Four hours. Raising it does not make a segment finish faster; a segment over the ceiling needs a GPU or a re-cadenced script, and the protocol's waits are not the thing to shorten because they exist so fights resolve.
_comment_cost_probe_frames: Frames the pre-flight times to measure what one costs here. Wall clock across real frames, not Performance.TIME_PROCESS, because the readback and PNG encode are most of the cost in capture mode and the CPU monitor does not see them. 20 frames is about 3.5 minutes under llvmpipe at 1920x1080 and under a second in logic mode.
_comment_cost_probe_budget_s: Added 2026-08-28 from the run-2 BLOCKER. The probe must not become the cost it is measuring. cost_probe_frames was written when a frame cost 6 ms, where 20 of them cost 0.12 s; the run-2 run measured 6.465 s per in-world frame under llvmpipe, at which price the same probe costs over two minutes -- and the re-price now runs after EVERY boot, not once. The probe stops as soon as it has both cost_probe_min_frames samples and this many seconds of elapsed time; the answer does not get better after that and the segment is paying for it.
_comment_cost_recheck_frames: Added 2026-08-28. How often, in physics frames actually ticked, a segment re-prices its REMAINDER against what frames are costing right now. Free by construction: it divides wall already spent by frames already ticked, so it needs no probe. It exists because a scene gets more expensive as the player walks into it, and because the world stand-up on a New Game is not a `boot` step -- S01's own run shows the in-play recheck catching 0.591 s/frame where no boot re-price could have.
_comment_cost_log_change_fraction: How far the measured frame cost has to move before a recheck earns a row in the ledger. A recheck every 120 frames over a 12,000-frame segment is a hundred rows saying the same 16.6 ms, which buries the two rows that matter and bloats every artefact carrying them. Boot re-prices and refusals are always kept, and `cost_rechecks` carries the count of the ones that were not, so the sampling stays auditable.
_comment_disk: Added 2026-08-28 from the run-2 BLOCKER's third finding: disk is a ceiling nobody had priced. At section H's planned cadences the eighteen segments were about 25 GB BEFORE the frame-cost multiplier, into a container with 23 GB free, and doubled again by the copy .git has to carry for the evidence to survive the container. The pre-flight now estimates bytes from a MEASURED PNG (its own self-test, at the real capture resolution) against a real `df`, and refuses a segment that cannot fit -- a hard refusal, like cost, that --gatef-allow-no-capture cannot waive. disk_reserve_bytes is what is left alone (2 GiB); disk_git_factor is 1.0 outside a work tree and applies only where git says the run directory is inside one. A df that cannot answer reads as NOT GATED, never as no room.
_comment_degenerate: A prescribed capture whose frame is this flat AND this dark is a photograph of an obstruction rather than of the game -- a camera inside geometry, a near field filled by something opaque, a fade caught mid-frame. Calibrated against X07's own 79 recovered frames, and the separation is not the one you would guess: mean luminance does NOT work, because the two DARKEST frames in that set are legitimate night captures. the_pond-night-gameplay is mean 25.1 / stddev 41.1 / 58.4% below luma 24; the_rise-gameplay is mean 26.6 / stddev 29.0 / 75.5% dark. The night frame is darker in the mean and still holds its contrast -- sky, moon, silhouette -- while the degenerate one is flat. So the test is dark fraction AND spread, both, and the thresholds sit between the two populations with the next-darkest of the other 75 frames at 0.284 / 48.8. The dark fraction tops out near 0.755 rather than 1.0 because the HUD is in the frame; these numbers are measured against that reality, not against a bare viewport.
